clue.text: Off on a trip

definitions.meaning: food that is off has gone bad, as meat or game left too long is said to be ...
under the influence of a hallucinogenic drug, intoxicated or stoned

explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses: game hung until gamey is high, and someone drugged is high.

clue.text: Rational development of simian touch, nothing less

indicators.note: a development reworks something into a new form, so these letters are rearranged
less means minus, so the letter for nothing is taken away from the word touch

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A biologist describes how an ape's sense of touch evolved by reason alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes O from TOUCH to leave TUCH; 'development of' rearranges SIMIAN plus TUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A humanistic outlook relies on human reason rather than faith, so it is rational in that philosophical sense.

clue.text: General award

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ..., the Union general of the American Civil War

explanation.definitionFit: A grant is something awarded, and Grant was a famous American general.

clue.text: As deep waves covering watercourse, one goes on foot

indicators.note: covering means one piece wraps round the other
waves suggests rippling movement, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: a rill is a small brook or stream

explanation.surface: Like deep waves rolling over a stream, something sets off on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' rearranges AS DEEP into ESPADE, and 'covering' wraps that round RILL.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe, so it is worn on, and goes on, a foot.

clue.text: Match in flame is blown out

indicators.note: something blown apart is scattered, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A match that is alight gets blown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown out' rearranges IN FLAME IS. 'Match' sits beside 'flame' to suggest a matchstick, but here it means a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A semifinal is a match, the round of a competition played just before the final.

clue.text: Tea service turned up under sofa, finally

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece placed under another follows it
finally points at the closing letter of the word sofa
in a down clue turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic church service

explanation.surface: A tea set has been overturned beneath a sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses MASS to SSAM, which goes under A, the last letter of sofa ('finally').
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea named after the Indian state where it grows.

clue.text: Artist has no name for instrument which Verdi may have put away

definitions.text: which Verdi may have put away

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual abbreviation for an artist

indicators.note: has no means the following letter is missing from the instrument

parts.note: a violin is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A painter swaps his name for a musical instrument the composer Verdi might have played and stored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' removes N from VIOLIN to leave VIOLI. To 'put away' food is to eat it, so the definition is a dish an Italian like Verdi might eat, not something he stored.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli is Italian stuffed pasta, the sort of dish the Italian composer Verdi might have eaten.

clue.text: Yale scholar — hairdresser?

definitions.meaning: an expert on Yale locks, someone who makes and repairs locks
jokingly, one who works locks of hair, as a smith works metal

explanation.definitionFit: A locksmith is an expert in Yale locks; read as lock-smith it is also a craftsman of hair locks.

clue.text: Attain sensitivity to music with Beethoven's Ninth

parts.note: having an ear for music means being sensitive to it

indicators.note: the ninth letter of the name Beethoven is wanted, not his symphony

explanation.surface: Someone achieves musical feeling through Beethoven's Ninth Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ninth' looks like the Choral Symphony but picks the ninth letter of BEETHOVEN, N.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn something is to gain or attain it through effort.

clue.text: Finally chart the most advance of theories

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps or charts

indicators.note: the letter furthest forward in the word, its first letter, is wanted

explanation.surface: A scholar maps the latest advance among theories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the most advance of' means the foremost letter of theories, T.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase at last means finally, after a long wait.

clue.text: When one has to eat, eat! Me slim? Unlikely!

indicators.note: unlikely says the words as given are improbable, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dieter told to eat protests that getting slim that way is unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlikely' rearranges EAT ME SLIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mealtimes are the set times when people eat their meals.

clue.text: One preaches through absorbing chapter four's conclusion

indicators.note: absorbing means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: via means by way of, through

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter, here of four

explanation.surface: A preacher works through to the end of chapter four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts C inside VIA, then R, the last letter of four ('conclusion'), follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest, someone whose job includes preaching sermons.

definitions.meaning: forty-nine per cent is not quite a half
an emphatic British exclamation meaning very much so, absolutely

explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'not half!' is an emphatic yes, as in 'Did you enjoy it? Not half!'
explanation.definitionFit: 49% falls short of half, while the British retort not half! means completely, so 100%.

clue.text: Film about a duck that's red

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a film is a thin layer or haze, a mist
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A film tells the story of a duck that happens to be red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and O inside MIST. 'Film' looks like a movie, but it is a haze.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maoist is a communist follower of Mao Zedong, and red is a standard term for a communist.

clue.text: Bitter fruits in this recreation area?

definitions.text: Bitter fruits in this recreation area?

parts.words: Bitter fruits in this recreation area?
parts.note: bitter is a British style of beer, and a garden is where fruits grow: a place outdoors where pints of bitter are drunk

explanation.surface: Sour fruit grows in a park.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER is a British pale beer, so 'bitter fruits' suggests beer growing in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer garden is an outdoor area at a pub where people relax over drinks.

clue.text: Construction to controversially write, perhaps?

parts.note: the phrase to write has an adverb pushed between its two words, the grammatical construction pedants object to

explanation.surface: A building project that is controversial to write about.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself demonstrates the construction: 'controversially' comes between 'to' and 'write'.
explanation.definitionFit: A split infinitive is a grammar construction in which a word separates to from its verb.

clue.text: Young ones disturb the filthy devil

parts.note: a litter is a group of young animals born together
to bug someone is to annoy or disturb them

explanation.surface: Children bother the dirty demon.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug is someone who carelessly drops rubbish, a messy nuisance.

clue.text: One beginning to rebel, taking heroin — one's gone off the rails

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word rebel

parts.note: someone who is on a drug is taking it
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A young rebel starts using heroin and goes off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'gone off the rails' means misbehaving; for the definition it means set off along the rails, as a train does.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron horse is an old name for a steam locomotive, which sets off along rails.

clue.text: Fifty into eight, to an odd number barely seen

annotationWithheld.why: Fifty into eight, to an odd number barely seen (2,3,10): the only parse is L (fifty) into an anagram ('odd') of EIGHT TO AN plus THREE, a synonym for 'number' scrambled with the clue's own words; THREE's letters are scattered through the answer so cannot be spelt beside it, and the check refuses both the stand-in anagram and the container-inside-anagram form
annotationWithheld.clue: Fifty into eight, to an odd number barely seen

clue.text: English reader, one with a voice

parts.note: a lector reads lessons aloud in church or lectures at a university

explanation.surface: An English reader has a fine voice.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector has a vote, and having a voice in a decision means having a say or vote.

clue.text: Head off kindly to bring son in as standard

indicators.note: to bring one thing into another puts it inside
in completes the instruction to place the letter inside
head off means the first letter is cut from the word

parts.note: benign means kindly, gentle

explanation.surface: A kindly man heads off to bring his son into line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' cuts B from BENIGN to leave ENIGN, and 'to bring ... in' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, and a standard is a flag or banner carried as an emblem.

clue.text: Remove the crown, and wear it oneself?

definitions.meaning: to cut off someone's head, the crown being the top of the head
to wear the crown yourself is to ... of state, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: To behead is to cut off the head; split as be head it means to be the ruler who wears the crown.

clue.text: General meaning to place division under duke

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece placed under another follows it

parts.note: a rift is a split or division

explanation.surface: A general aims to put a split below the duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer, but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of something is its general sense or gist.

clue.text: Exclamation of joy as girl's put on brief underwear

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece put on another is added after it
brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights, worn as underwear
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's delighted shout as she pulls on short underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims the last letter and 'put on' adds the girl after it. 'brief' also hints at briefs, the underwear, which is not its job here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a cry of praise or joy, used in worship.

clue.text: Fool about making constituent gunpowder

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An idiot fools about making explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, potassium nitrate or saltpetre, is the main ingredient of gunpowder.

clue.text: One going off to make fortune

definitions.meaning: an explosive device detonates, or goes off
a ... is British slang for a lot of money, as in costing a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A bomb goes off, and in British slang something that costs a bomb costs a fortune.

clue.text: Gold piece for heavenly passage

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A golden coin offered for the soul's journey to heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is the path a body follows around a star or planet in the heavens.

clue.text: Appearing washed out, I considered ringing doctor

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding one piece with the other

parts.note: rated means considered or judged
to doctor something is to rig it, to falsify it

explanation.surface: Looking pale, a man decides to phone his doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' places one piece inside the other. 'doctor' looks like a physician but is a verb: to fix or falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrigated means washed out with a flow of liquid, as a wound is cleaned.

clue.text: Trouble about Britain in Ireland, a dictatorial controller

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: bother means trouble or fuss

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: GB, Great Britain

explanation.surface: Trouble over British rule in Ireland, under an autocratic governor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'about' make a container within a container. IR is the abbreviation for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Brother is the all-seeing ruler of Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, now a byword for an authoritarian controller.

clue.text: Winger playing part in international

indicators.note: playing a part in suggests the answer is a part of the following word

explanation.surface: A winger plays a role in an international match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a football player on the wing, but it means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A tern is a seabird, and a winger is a crossword word for any winged creature.
